primary_category.subcategory: A2.4 Information search, retrieval, gathering, and evaluation

evidence.quote: Three publishers submitted proposals — Curriculum A, B, and C. Each had a standards-alignment matrix, sample units, vendor support materials
evidence.explanation: The core work of the episode is gathering and reviewing proposal documents from competing vendors.

evidence.quote: someone mentioned a statistical pilot report from a comparable district, covering multiple schools over a full year
evidence.explanation: Retrieving and evaluating a statistical evidence source is a direct information-search/evaluation act.

evidence.quote: Everyone submitted rubric scores across five criteria for all three curricula
evidence.explanation: Scoring against a rubric is an evaluative information-processing task comparing options against criteria.

evidence.quote: With twelve weeks, we had every intention of giving all three a genuinely deep look before narrowing anything down
evidence.explanation: Sequencing a multi-week adoption cycle, allocating review time across three options, and deciding narrowing strategy constitutes planning toward a goal.

evidence.quote: We ran a three-week pilot of Curriculum B in two schools
evidence.explanation: Designing and running a pilot program is a non-routine problem-resolution activity requiring anticipation of dependencies (classroom assignment, timing, observation).

evidence.quote: Curriculum A had an odd split on differentiated-instruction support — two very high scores, two very low. B's scores were tighter across the board... The scores just got averaged straight across
evidence.explanation: Computing and interpreting composite numeric scores from rubric ratings is a quantitative reasoning task.

evidence.quote: When the chair compiled them... The chair still needed one composite number per curriculum for the board memo
evidence.explanation: The chair coordinates the aggregation of individual committee members' scores into a single group output for an external stakeholder (the board), reflecting organizational coordination.

evidence.quote: our first working session ended up centered on B
evidence.explanation: Deciding collective allocation of committee working-session time across options reflects coordination of shared group activity.

evidence.quote: I'd flag any criterion with a wide spread and ask why before folding it into one number. The spread itself was telling us something.
evidence.explanation: The participant generalises from the episode to a revised principle for evaluating rubric disagreement, an abstraction beyond the immediate facts.

all_observed_categories: A2.4 Information search, retrieval, gathering, and evaluation
not_observed_or_insufficient: A1.1 Strength - no physical exertion described
A1.2 Dexterity - no fine motor manipulation described
A1.3 Navigation - no spatial movement task described beyond passing mention of classroom observation not undertaken
A3.1 Serving and attending - no direct service-to-client interaction described
A3.2 Teaching, training, and coaching - committee members are described as teachers elsewhere but this episode does not depict instructional activity
A3.5 Caring - no welfare-support interaction described

A3.3 Selling and influencing - vendor reps engage in persuasion but the participant's own task is receiving/evaluating, not persuading; borderline but insufficiently evidenced for the participant's own role
ambiguities: A3.3 Selling and influencing could arguably apply to the vendor's conduct ('Curriculum B's rep brought in committee members from other districts using it') but this describes the vendor's action upon the participant, not the participant's own task, so it was excluded from the participant's task classification.

A2.2 Literacy (reading proposals, rubric materials) is clearly present as a substrate activity but is subsumed under A2.4 information evaluation as the more specific and central category for this episode; listed in all_observed_categories but not elevated to a separate secondary category to avoid redundancy with A2.4.

evidence.quote: We had time. It's just that once people were talking about what the neighboring district found, B became the thing everyone wanted to dig into first.
evidence.explanation: The committee self-determines its own review sequence, depth, and pacing without an externally imposed procedure dictating those choices.

evidence.quote: We didn't send anyone to observe the second pilot classroom, even though we had the calendar space to do that easily.
evidence.explanation: The committee had discretion to pursue further investigation but chose not to, indicating latitude over methods and depth of inquiry.

evidence.quote: the superintendent's office asked us to run a full adoption cycle for a new K-8 math curriculum
evidence.explanation: The committee's mandate originates from and is ultimately accountable to the superintendent's office and board.

evidence.quote: The board notice? They asked. Why a criterion with that much internal disagreement got reported as one clean number.
evidence.explanation: The board reviews and questions the committee's output, indicating an external oversight/monitoring layer on the committee's work product.

evidence.quote: two of our members came back from a regional math conference... Our people came back energized
evidence.explanation: Committee decisions are shaped by shared information brought back by members and collective working sessions.

evidence.quote: Everyone submitted rubric scores across five criteria for all three curricula. When the chair compiled them...
evidence.explanation: The final decision output depends on pooling individual contributions from multiple committee members into one collective product.

evidence.quote: the superintendent's office asked us to run a full adoption cycle for a new K-8 math curriculum
evidence.explanation: Curriculum adoption cycles are described as periodic (roughly every several years, occurring with a shifted six-to-twelve-week calendar), not a frequently recurring daily task.

evidence.quote: Everyone submitted rubric scores across five criteria for all three curricula
evidence.explanation: A shared rubric with fixed criteria indicates a standardized evaluation procedure, though how disagreements are handled is not standardized.

evidence.quote: Each had a standards-alignment matrix, sample units, vendor support materials, the usual package
evidence.explanation: The phrase 'the usual package' indicates a recurring, prescribed proposal-submission format.

evidence.quote: it showed mixed results across schools, not the clean win the anecdote suggested
evidence.explanation: Outcome evidence for the options was ambiguous and not fully predictable in advance, though the overall adoption process and its steps were known in advance.

evidence.quote: one of the pilot teachers flagged pacing problems in a unit — said the sequencing didn't match how her students were actually progressing
evidence.explanation: An unplanned pilot-teacher concern arose mid-process, requiring the committee to respond to an unanticipated development, though the response given was minimal.

tools.role_in_task: Compiling and averaging rubric scores into a spreadsheet for the board memo

evidence.quote: It went into the spreadsheet like everything else.
evidence.explanation: A spreadsheet, a basic office-software tool, is used to record and aggregate scores.

tools.role_in_task: Not clearly evidenced as a distinct specialised software system beyond general office tools

evidence.quote: a standards-alignment matrix, sample units, vendor support materials
evidence.explanation: Vendor-provided alignment matrices may originate from specialised curriculum-review platforms, but the interview does not describe the participant operating any such system directly, so confidence is low.
